title: Scheduled atomic transfer sanity check and priority-shed procedure for active-passive DR drills
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Run an orchestrated, repeatable active→passive transfer that validates backup/restore integrity, KV/prefix cache reconciliation, tokenstore quiesce, and progressive priority-based load-shedding. The goal is to prove an atomic transfer window for latency-sensitive tenants while exercising circuit-breaker and surge-shed choreography. This ticket owns the drill runbook, test harness automation, telemetry gates, and post-mortem template for scheduled rehearsals.
playbook_steps: Pre-drill: notify stakeholders (SRE, platform, on-call, security, customer success) and post maintenance window in Status page
Snapshot: trigger consistent point-in-time KV snapshot and tokenstore export; compute checksums and fingerprint manifests
Quiesce: pause background compaction and non-critical scheduled jobs on active region; mark route as drain-ready
Traffic taper: apply staged weight reduction to active region with 90s holdpoints and synthetic traffic validation at each stage
Atomic cutover: flip router at regional control-plane to passive region while enabling canary routing to 5% of production traffic
KV reconcile: run prefix-hash compare between restored snapshot and live passive store; run incremental replayer for missing deltas
Circuit breaker probe: simulate high-latency backend call and confirm circuit opens/fails over to fallback tier
Priority shed: apply priority-based token bucket thresholds and sequentially shed non-critical routes (embeddings batch jobs, low-tier ML inference) while measuring latencies for P0 clients
Soak: keep passive region serving for 30 minutes under reduced load with synthetic and sampled production traces
Rollback or Promote: decision point based on acceptance criteria — either rollback traffic to original active region or promote passive to primary and run post-promote tasks
Post-drill: run integrity audit, publish telemetry summary, and capture lessons in post-mortem template
acceptance_criteria: All KV snapshot checksums match within defined tolerances, or documented reconciliation steps executed successfully
SLOs for P0 routes remain within doubled latency budget during the atomic transfer window
Circuit breaker behaviour observed and confirmed (open, fallback, closed) according to the runbook tests
Priority-based load shedding reduces non-critical request volume by at least 70% without violating P0 availability targets
Automated runbook scripts finish without manual intervention for non-exception paths
Post-drill audit contains a reconciled timeline, binary pass/fail flags for each gating check, and next-action items
telemetry_checks: Compare per-route latency p95/p99 pre-cutover vs during-cutover
KV snapshot byte-level checksum match and missing keys count
Error budget burn-rate for the hour surrounding the cutover
Circuit-breaker open-rate and fallback invocation count
Queue length / backlog for batch workers after shed begins
rollback_steps: Immediate: abort promotion and flip router weights back to active region
Rehydrate: if passive had mutated data, run a replay/merge job using snapshot deltas collected during promotion
Circuit reset: clear in-flight circuit-breaker timers and allow controlled re-introduction of shed routes
Validate: re-run checksum and tokenstore sanity checks after rollback
Post-incident: capture root cause, adjust runbook step timing or thresholds, escalate if data divergence occurred
automation_tasks: Add a scripted kv-snapshot + fingerprint generator to infra-scripts (PR linked)
Extend runbook CLI to accept --priority-shed-profile and --soak-duration flags
Create synthetic traffic manifests that mirror production route mix for 15m windows
Add an alert that gates promotion if checksum mismatch > 0
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: long replay time for KV deltas causing extended CT (cutover time). Mitigation: pre-warm incremental replayer and parallelize read streams
Risk: tokenstore restore latency prevents auth for clients. Mitigation: staged route lift with auth bypass for internal canaries and progressive traffic ramp
Risk: incorrect shed policy impacts paying customers. Mitigation: enforce canaryed priority rules and manual approval for full-shed escalation
Risk: cascading circuit-breaker opens after cutover. Mitigation: adaptive retry-backoff and service-level CB thresholds tuned in test harness
postmortem_template: Gates: each acceptance criterion with pass/fail and evidence links
Telemetry: snapshot of key metrics and diffs
Root cause analysis and contributing factors
Action items: owner, estimate, and due date

Coordinate with Sales/CS for a small set of customers who may observe degraded performance during the drill
Document all manual overrides and keep them to a minimum — every manual step increases learning value
